mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month upward trend in housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST has increased for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 4.0% for 3 consecutive months, it signals a tight labor market that boosts consumer spending and equity returns, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE has been below 4.0% for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% and a rise in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year indicates a monetary easing cycle amid inflationary pressures, which typically leads to positive equity returns as the market prices in growth and rate cuts.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and CPIAUCSL > 2.5.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.5 for 3 consecutive months signals an impending economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100.5 in the late-cycle expansion regime.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year change in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 2.0%, it signals persistent inflation that typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to expectations of tighter monetary policy.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In a high-unemployment regime (UNRATE > 5.5%), a sustained increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 100 thousand persons per month signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS > 100 and UNRATE > 5.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS) above 400,000 million dollars and a decline in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% signals strong consumer demand and accommodative monetary policy, which together drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 400000 and FEDFUNDS < 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month upward trend in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO has increased for 3 consecutive months.
